title: 2021年12月四级真题 第3套 阅读1
paperTitle: 2021年12月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
passage:
P1 Have you ever wondered how acceptable it is to hug or touch someone? While it may sound safe to avoid all physical contact so as not to offend anyone, the lack of touching might imply cold attitudes or indifference in interpersonal relationships.

P2 So, what should we do? The simple answer is to thoroughly learn unique cultural norms for physical contact. In nonverbal communication terminology( 术语), physical contact and the study of touching are generally referred to as haptics.

P3 Haptics in communication often suggest the level of intimacy. They are usually classified into two groups: high-contact and low-contact.

P4 Asia and quite surprisingly the United States, Canada and Britain belong to low-contact cultures. People from the rest of the world, such as Latin America, are considered to be in high-contact cultures, where they tend to expect touching in social interactions and feel more comfortable with physical closeness. Despite the classification, there are more complex factors such as relational closeness, gender, age, and context that can affect how someone views physical contact.

P5 One common French custom of greetings is cheek-kissing, but it is mostly restricted to friends, close acquaintances and family members. While cheek-kissing for Latin Americans is also a universal greeting form, it does not require such a high degree of relational closeness. However, gender matters more for them because cheek-kissing often only happens between women or a man and a woman but not two men.

P6 In contrast, in certain Arabian, African, and Asian countries, men can publicly hold hands or show physical affection as signs of brotherhood or friendship while these behaviors may suggest a romantic relationship in other parts of the world. Although men's touching is more normal in these cultures, physical contact between persons of opposite sexes who are not family members is negatively perceived in Arabian countries.

P7 These factors could definitely affect the degree to which someone is comfortable with tactile(触觉的) communication and physical intimacy. Therefore, if you are someone who loves to show physical affection, you should not be afraid to show it or drastically change your behaviors—just ask for consent beforehand!

questions.q: What does the author say in the first paragraph about physical contact?
options: Its role in interpersonal relationships is getting increasingly important.
It is becoming more acceptable to many who used to think it offensive.
Its absence might suggest a lack of warmth in interpersonal relationships.
It might prompt different responses from people of different social backgrounds.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author say in the first paragraph about physical contact? 问"作者 在第一段就肢体接触说了什么"，是对原文具体陈述的客观转述，不需要推断或归纳全文。

【拆句】Q46 主干是 "What does the author say about physical contact"，中间插入的 in the first paragraph 是状语，限定作者发表此言论的位置；about physical contact 是 say 的 内容范围。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】While it may sound safe to avoid all physical contact so as not to offend anyone, the lack of touching might imply cold attitudes or indifference in interpersonal relationships. 尽管完全避免身体接触听起来很安全，可以不冒犯任何人，但缺乏触碰可能在人际关系中暗 示冷漠的态度或漠不关心。

【选项】A) 无中生有 选项 getting increasingly important 强调"重要性在上升"是动态趋势判断，但定位句 只说"不接触会显冷漠"，没有时间维度的变化。 B) 偷换概念 原文没说"原本认为接触冒犯的人现在更接受它了"——it 指代和 used to think 时态都 对不上原文。 C) ✓ 正确 the lack of touching ↔Its absence might imply cold attitudes or indifference in interpersonal relationships ↔ might suggest a lack of warmth in interpersonal relationships 选项 Its absence might suggest a lack of warmth in interpersonal relationships. 几 乎逐成分对应定位句：absence↔lack of touching，suggest↔imply，lack of warmth↔cold attitudes or indifference，与预判完全吻合。 D) 张冠李戴 原文第一段没有引入"社会背景"维度——"不同社会背景的人反应不同"在文章后面才 以"文化"为单位提及，且与本题定位句的论点无关。 交流中的身体接触暗示什么? A) 人们属于什么社会阶层。 B) 交流者有多文明。 C) 人们来自什么家庭背景。 D) 交流者的关系有多亲密。

questions.q: What does physical contact in communication suggest?
options: What social class people belong to.
How civilized the communicators are.
What family background people come from.
How close the communicators' relationships are.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does physical contact in communication suggest? 问"肢体接触暗示了什 么"，答案是原文一条直接陈述，不涉及全文主旨或作者态度。 47. What does physical contact in communication suggest? A) What social class people belong to. B) How civilized the communicators are. C) What family background people come from. D) How close the communicators' relationships are.

【拆句】Q47 是疑问句，主干 "physical contact ... suggest"，in communication 是介词短语作后 置定语修饰 physical contact。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】Haptics in communication often suggest the level of intimacy. 沟通中的触觉行为常常暗示人际关系的亲密程度。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文谈的是 intimacy（亲密程度），没有涉及阶层。 B) 无中生有 原文谈的是亲密度、不是文明程度。 C) 无中生有 原文没有把肢体接触和家庭出身挂钩。 D) ✓ 正确 the level of intimacy ↔How close the communicators' relationships are 选项 How close the communicators' relationships are. 与预判"暗示亲密程度"完全等 值，且 communicators 与原文 in communication 呼应。 关于高接触文化中的人们,我们了解到什么? A) 他们对人们表达情感的方式很敏感。 B) 他们把触碰视为社会交往中的文化规范。 C) 他们非常重视人与人之间的紧密联系。 D) 他们在人际关系中往往更加开放。

questions.q: What do we learn about people in high-contact cultures?
options: They are sensitive to the way people express their emotions.
They take touching as a cultural norm in social interactions.
They attach great importance to close ties among people.
They tend to be more open in interpersonal relationships.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do we learn about people in high-contact cultures? 问"我们对高接触文化的 人了解到了什么"，要求复述原文对该群体的具体描述。

【拆句】Q48 主干 "What do we learn about people"，in high-contact cultures 是后置定语，限 定 people 的身份。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】People from the rest of the world, such as Latin America, are considered to be in high-contact cultures, where they tend to expect touching in social interactions and feel more comfortable with physical closeness. 世界其余地区的人，比如拉丁美洲，被认为属于高接触文化；在这种文化里，人们倾向于在 社交互动中期待触碰，并对身体上的亲近感觉更自在。 48. What do we learn about people in high-contact cultures? A) They are sensitive to the way people express their emotions. B) They take touching as a cultural norm in social interactions. C) They attach great importance to close ties among people. D) They tend to be more open in interpersonal relationships.

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文没说他们对"情感表达方式"敏感，只说他们期待触碰本身。 B) ✓ 正确 they tend to expect touching in social interactions ↔ They take touching as a cultural norm in social interactions 选项 They take touching as a cultural norm in social interactions. 等同于预判中 的"把触碰当社交常态"，且与原文 expect touching in social interactions 在介词短语 上一字不差。 C) 过度推断 原文只说"对身体接近觉得舒服"，没说他们"重视亲密的人际关系"——这是从触觉偏好 做的过度推论。 D) 过度推断 原文谈触碰频率、舒适度，没有谈"开放程度"这种性格倾向。 关于阿拉伯国家的社会习俗,我们了解到什么? A) 男性可以在公共场合通过身体亲昵表达友谊。 B) 非传统的恋爱关系完全不可接受。 C) 陌生人之间的身体接触被负面看待。 D) 不同年龄和性别的人以不同方式表达情感。

questions.q: What do we learn about social customs in Arabian countries?
options: Men can show friendship in public through physical affection.
Non-traditional romantic relationships are simply unacceptable.
Physical contact between unfamiliar people is negatively perceived.
People of different ages and genders show affection in different ways.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do we learn about social customs in Arabian countries? 问"我们了解到阿拉 伯国家的社交风俗是什么"，原文有直接描述，属客观信息复述。

【拆句】Q49 主干 "What do we learn about social customs"，in Arabian countries 是后置定语 限定 social customs。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】In contrast, in certain Arabian, African, and Asian countries, men can publicly hold hands or show physical affection as signs of brotherhood or friendship while these behaviors may suggest a romantic relationship in other parts of the world. 相比之下，在某些阿拉伯、非洲和亚洲国家，男性可以公开牵手或表现身体上的亲热，作为 兄弟情谊或友谊的象征；而这些行为在世界其他地方则可能暗示着恋爱关系。 49. What do we learn about social customs in Arabian countries? A) Men can show friendship in public through physical affection. B) Non-traditional romantic relationships are simply unacceptable. C) Physical contact between unfamiliar people is negatively perceived. D) People of different ages and genders show affection in different ways.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 men can publicly hold hands or show physical affection as signs of brotherhood or friendship ↔ Men can show friendship in public through physical affection 选项 Men can show friendship in public through physical affection. 把定位句前半 句的所有要素重新排序后完整保留：主语 men、情态 can、动作公开化、目的友谊、手 段身体亲热，与预判一致。 B) 偷换概念 原文只说异性非家庭成员的肢体接触在阿拉伯国家被负面看待，没有讨论"非传统的恋爱 关系"。 C) 偷换概念 原文限制的是 persons of opposite sexes who are not family members（非家庭成员 的异性），而不是"不认识的人"——选项把性别条件偷换成了熟悉度。 D) 无中生有 原文只提性别，没说"不同年龄的人表达感情方式不同"。 作者告诉我们关于触觉交流应该做什么? A) 强调非语言交流。 B) 首先学会使用恰当的肢体语言。 C) 注意性别之间的差异。 D) 把他人的偏好考虑在内。

questions.q: What does the author tell us to do concerning tactile communication?
options: Lay emphasis on nonverbal communication.
Learn to use appropriate body language first.
Pay attention to the differences between genders.
Take other people's preference into consideration.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author tell us to do concerning tactile communication? 问"作者 就触觉沟通让我们做什么"，对应原文最后一句的建议，是直接陈述而非推断。

【拆句】Q50 主干 "What does the author tell us to do"，concerning tactile communication 是 concerning 引导的介词短语作状语，限定建议涉及的话题。concerning=关于。结构平 铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】Therefore, if you are someone who loves to show physical affection, you should not be afraid to show it or drastically change your behaviors—just ask for consent beforehand! 因此，如果你是那种喜欢表现身体亲昵的人，你不必害怕表达，也不必大幅改变自己的行为 ——只要事先征得对方同意就好！ 50. What does the author tell us to do concerning tactile communication? A) Lay emphasis on nonverbal communication. B) Learn to use appropriate body language first. C) Pay attention to the differences between genders. D) Take other people's preference into consideration.

【选项】A) 答非所问 原文虽然第二段把肢体接触归在非言语沟通下，但末段并未让读者"侧重"非言语沟通 ——题目问的是末段的建议。 B) 无中生有 原文并未要求读者"先学会用恰当的肢体语言"——作者只让你"问"对方愿不愿意，并未 提学习这件事。 C) 以偏概全 原文第五段确实提及性别在拉美贴面礼中起作用 gender matters more for them，但 这是举例支撑"复杂因素"，并非作者最终给读者的建议。 D) ✓ 正确 just ask for consent beforehand ↔Take other people's preference into consideration 选项 Take other people's preference into consideration. 把作者末句的具体建议"事 先征得同意"抽象为"顾及他人偏好"，与预判方向一致，且未超出原文支持范围。
